reference is `desktop/main.ts`, which opens the full hosted application in
Electrobun at 1280 × 860. Matching the reference includes its styling, original
assets, interaction states, documents, and connected workflows.

The current offline editor and independent foundations are partial delivery.
The full styling, asset and behavior port remains unfinished; scoped checks do
not establish completion of the desktop experience.

# Twyne GPUI

Twyne's native desktop port uses Rust and [GPUI Kit 0.7](https://gpui-kit.com/).
The goal is the full hosted desktop experience with identical styling, original
assets and behavior. The working offline slice includes the rich editor, Dossier,
local editorial panels and native Typst proof/PDF.

The full Electrobun application remains the reference. The port is unfinished;
[PORT_PLAN.md](PORT_PLAN.md) separates implemented behavior, retained checks,
unmounted foundations and remaining work.

[ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) maps native packages to their original web
counterparts, records ownership boundaries, and gives focused investigation checks.

## Run

Use Bun, the repository's Rust toolchain, and the native libraries in
[GPUI Kit's installation guide](https://gpui-kit.com/docs/installation/).
The repository's Devenv shell provides the Rust toolchain and Linux libraries.

From the repository root:

```bash
rtk proxy bun install --frozen-lockfile
rtk proxy devenv shell -- rtk proxy bun run desktop.gpui
```

Use an isolated library or import files on startup:

```bash
rtk proxy devenv shell -- rtk proxy bun run desktop.gpui --data-dir /tmp/twyne-native-library /path/to/draft.typ
```

Imports create library copies. Original files remain independent.

The developer build creates `twyne-document` from Twyne's existing TypeScript
document converters. Its compiled executable includes the Bun runtime. Offline
writing needs no web server or account; GPUI renders the interface and the native
Rust Typst engine renders proof/PDF. The helper handles source/HTML reconciliation,
starter generation and the original MathJax export conversion.

The helper build also creates `twyne-math-write`. It is a diagnostic executable,
not the main editor's math renderer or evidence of Write-view parity.

For direct Cargo development, build the helper first:

```bash
rtk proxy bun run desktop.gpui.build-helper
rtk proxy devenv shell -- rtk proxy cargo run --locked --manifest-path desktop/gpui/Cargo.toml
```

Linux requires X11 or Wayland and a graphics driver supported by WGPU. Native
file pickers use the desktop's XDG portal. macOS requires Xcode command line
tools; Windows requires the MSVC C++ toolchain. Bundles, installers, signing, and
automatic updates remain pending.

## Writing and proof

- **Write:** native rich text with Unicode input, selection, clipboard, IME,
  formatting, and undo/redo. Typing bursts form one undo group. Imported cached
  HTML is projected from canonical source before editing. Footnote and endnote
  markers open an editable note; collected notes navigate back to their
  manuscript references. Save and navigation capture unblurred note input.
- **Equation source:** activate an inline or block equation to edit its retained native textarea. Render equation submits through the actual canonical converter and preserves independent manuscript undo; Cancel keeps the saved source. Inline editing uses a measured child inside the original atom. Preview currently reports unavailable. Actual OS input and original-browser baseline/pixel parity remain separate gates.
- **Dossier:** the original ten sections, imported material, references, local
  probes, create/refine filing, and scoped recovery. Filing opens Write after
  the document is actually saved.
- **Source:** canonical Typst with a separate recoverable draft. Apply requires
  a successful current compile and verified projection. Discard preserves the
  manuscript. Source edits update the real proof after 450 ms of quiet. The
  native code editor provides Typst highlighting, line numbers,
  folded generated helpers, search/replace, source snippets, comments, wrapping,
  and line navigation. Pending Source edits lock the rich view.
- **Proof/Split:** the same pinned Typst fork and ordered fonts as the web
  renderer, original artwork, real SVG pages, zoom, page navigation, and PDF
  export. Failed compilation retains the last valid proof.
  The footer retains the selected page across Write/Proof transitions. Its
  count option leaves the current mode active; page choices reveal the page's
  top, and a shorter valid proof falls back to the count option.
  Closed Arrow/Home/End and PageUp/PageDown keys retain native focus. The
  combobox exposes its selected label and actual popup open state.
  Typed page labels retain focus; repeated letters cycle matching labels and
  search expires after the original one-second pause. Space continues an
  active prefix or opens the popup when search is idle.
- **Compositor:** Home, Insert, Review, and View controls act on the native
  document. Arrow keys change tabs and retain native focus through wrapping;
  Undo/Redo use the actual manuscript history and respect read-only mode.
  Page settings and header/footer text are saved with the folio.
  The page ruler changes the actual margins through drag or keyboard input.
  Optional native pagination has physical-page and input checks; the current
  web editor route does not register its existing pagination engine, so this
  does not establish matching active-route behavior.
  Local PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP files become portable offline images; choosing a file
  retains the original bytes and one undo restores the preceding manuscript.
  File insertion checks the original converter in the background first: a
  valid image that exceeds the 5 MB Typst editing limit leaves the draft intact.
  Connected actions stay disabled until their native adapters exist.
- **Appearance:** original presets and colour overrides preview immediately
  and persist separately from manuscript formatting. Save failures retain the
  preview and expose a retry; the stored System choice follows OS appearance.
- **Versions:** local checkpoints and passage comparisons in the Editorial
  Board. Restore saves the current manuscript first and refuses to replace
  typing or Source edits made while a restore is being prepared. Saved status
  follows the actual durable write.
- **Cast:** the Room of Editors, local roster and assistance settings, retained
  editorial notes/replies, and saved Full Analysis use the original profiles
  and assets. The Board, roster page and analysis page share one retained room.
  Local writer replies can be filed without contacting a provider. Unfinished
  replies and roster forms survive navigation and closing; failed writes hold
  the exact request and block departure until retry. Existing analyses can be
  copied or downloaded. Provider notes, proposed edits, new analyses, spoken
  notes and persona-mark navigation remain unavailable.
- **Rubric:** local weights, custom criteria and retained grades share the
  Board and Galley. Changes follow the actual durable write, and a failed save
  keeps its candidate for retry. New provider grading remains unavailable.
- **Apparatus:** saved sources share the Board and full page. Local scans use
  the original citation rules; Copy publishes only the active folio's sources.
  Cite inserts an undoable footnote and saves the manuscript before confirming
  its source timestamp. Failed metadata writes retain a retry without repeating

# Remote GPUI builds

Desktop builds, tests and captures run on Railway sandboxes in the
`twyne-gpui-builds` project. Each port lane has its own sandbox and runs
detached jobs, so an agent can start a build and keep working:

```sh
bun run desktop.gpui.job start . --lane <lane> --pull 'desktop/gpui/target/parity/**' -- <command...>
bun run desktop.gpui.job status <lane>          # running | finished N | interrupted | none
bun run desktop.gpui.job logs <lane> --lines 80 # tail of the output
bun run desktop.gpui.job pull . --lane <lane>   # copy --pull files and remote-job.log back
bun run desktop.gpui.job stop <lane>            # destroy the lane's sandbox
bun run desktop.gpui.job list                   # lanes and their sandboxes
```

## How it works

- **Running commands.** Commands run inside `devenv shell` in `/root/work`,
  so they use the pinned toolchain.
- **Syncing.** Each `start` streams the worktree's tracked and unignored files
  in. Launch videos and audio are left out. Files are compared by content, so
  unchanged files keep their timestamps and Cargo rebuilds only what the lane
  edited.
- **Checkpoints.** New lanes boot from the `twyne-gpui-warm` checkpoint. It
  already has dependencies installed, the document helper built, and the
  `ui-tests` binary and tests compiled.
  - Rebuild it after large changes on the integration branch with
    `bun desktop/gpui/tools/remote/railway.ts warm <worktree>`.
  - `twyne-gpui-base` holds just the toolchain: the apt libraries, Nix and
    devenv 2.4.0.
- **Lane records** are one file per lane in `~/.config/twyne/railway-lanes/`.
  A shared JSON file lost entries when many lanes created sandboxes at once.
- **Memory and disk.** Jobs build with four parallel jobs: sandboxes have
  7 GB of RAM plus about 1.3 GB of zram swap. Don't add a swapfile. The
  29 GB disk holds the Nix store (about 8 GB) and the build tree (about 10 GB),
  and an 8 GB swapfile filled it. Jobs also build with `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` and
  clear Bun's download cache, which together free about 5 GB, and log the free
  space before building.
- **Browser captures.** Each job downloads Playwright's Chromium on its first
  run in a sandbox.
- **Idle timeout.** Sandboxes are destroyed after 120 idle minutes, so stop
  your lane when done.

The E2B runner (`run.ts`, `job.ts`, `warm.ts`, `rewarm.ts`) is retired and
refuses to start jobs.

---
name: typst-compiler-constraints
description: "Twyne's web Typst is 0.14.x via typst.ts 0.7.0; Universe packages resolve via a prefetching registry (2026-10-23), desktop GPUI does not; packages needing 0.15 fail"
metadata:
  type: project
---

`@myriaddreamin/typst.ts` 0.7.0 ships a WASM compiler at Typst 0.14.x. As of 2026-10-23 the web worker
(`src/utils/typst/compiler.worker.ts`) resolves `#import "@preview/..."` through `TwynePackageRegistry`
in `src/utils/typst/packages.ts`. Archives (and their transitive imports) are prefetched async before
compiling, because the compiler's resolve is synchronous, and kept in Cache Storage.

**Why:** Packages whose `compiler` field is above 0.14 (codly 2.0, touying 0.8, min-book, cheq) still
cannot compile; the editor's package autocomplete filters them out (`TYPST_COMPILER_VERSION`). The desktop
GPUI app compiles with its own Rust `OfflineWorld`, which has no package resolution.

**How to apply:** Check a package's `compiler` field in `https://packages.typst.org/preview/index.json`
before recommending it. Package work for desktop means adding a resolver to `desktop/gpui/src/native_typst.rs`.

Source format: since 2026-10-23 saved source is idiomatic Typst with no inline preamble; helpers
(`TYPST_HELPERS`) are injected at typeset time, and `migrateTypstSource` upgrades old
`// twyne-document:1` drafts.

content.text:
I merged the latest web work into the GPUI port and added the right-click menu. Both are committed locally on `feat/native-port-ai-audio`; nothing is pushed. The web changes still break 4 native checks, which I haven't fixed yet.

**Where the port is:** it lives on `feat/native-port-ai-audio` (worktree `~/Projects/worktrees/twyne-native-port-20261028`), not `feat/clairic-extraction`. Nobody had touched it since Oct 29, and it was 66 web commits behind.

**What I did:**
- **Merged `feat/clairic-extraction` into the port** (`907ae29d`). Only `bun.lock` conflicted, and I regenerated it.
- **Fixed what the merge broke:**
  - The native document helper wouldn't build because the web moved `htmlToPlainText` into its own module. It now imports it from there.
  - The new-document starter on the web now opens with just the title. I updated the native test to expect that.
  - Asset and steering fixtures were re-synced. Only their recorded source hashes changed; no colours or values did.
  - The Railway build compiles the merged branch cleanly.
- **Right-click menu** (`e93c605e`, in `desktop/gpui/src/editor/view_context_menu.rs`):
  - It offers Cut / Copy / Paste, Bold / Italic / Underline, Comment on selection, Undo / Redo and Select all.
  - Every item runs the editor's existing command, so behaviour matches the keyboard shortcuts.
  - Right-clicking outside the current selection moves the caret to the click point first. Right-clicking inside it keeps the selection.
  - Read-only documents offer only Copy and Select all.
  - "Comment on selection" opens the same margin-note composer as the Comment button in the Review tab.
  - A new test right-clicks the real editor and clicks the menu item. The editor and app tests pass (207), and I added the menu to the README.

**Full native test suite:** 1122 passed, 9 failed. None of the failures are in the editor.
- **4 are caused by the new web changes:**
  - The in-flow tool rules (`in-flow-tools.ts`), the struggle tracker (`struggle-tracker.ts`, largely rewritten) and the struggle signals (`struggle-signals.ts`) changed on the web, so the native copies are out of date.
  - Plain Typst export no longer matches the web output, because the web now writes plain Typst source and adds Twyne's helpers only when compiling.
  - Fixing these means porting the new web logic to Rust, not just updating stored hashes.
- **5 were already failing before the merge:** Dossier provider form, House keyboard focus, AI model settings, writer name saved on blur, and the voice recorder. The last full run on Oct 29 failed the same 5.

**Disk:** `/home` is at 100% (8.8 GB free). The port's build folder takes 8.3 GB. Any further heavy builds should run on Railway, or you could clear old worktrees.

**Not ported yet:** most of the visible web features since Oct 29, including the persona cards and faces on note anchors, the speaker card on hover, the local Live voice, readable narration errors, account settings and export, and the shared document header.

Should I start on the 4 web-change failures next, or on those features? They split into separate pieces of work, so I could run them in parallel as remote Terra lanes.
